user_questions.question: Which fields should 'locations' map between? (A, recommended) Lead.Number_of_Locations__c Number(5,0), the merchant field created with Cuisine/POS -> Account.NumberofLocations__c (widened to 5 digits); (B) Lead.NumberofLocations__c Number(3,0), the sample field on the Lead Sales/Marketing layouts -> Account.NumberofLocations__c; (C) either Lead field -> Account.Total_Storefronts__c Number(18,0). Evidence: both Lead fields are labelled 'Number of Locations' and hold no data on any of the 5 Leads.

skill_friction: The simulated answer fixed the target (Account.NumberofLocations__c) but named the source only by label, which both Lead fields share. The 'map to the option its words match' rule matched two options; I tagged the choice as an assumption, but SKILL.md does not say what to do when an answer matches more than one option.

LeadConvertSettings cannot be read, so the core row had to be Conditional (retrieve and merge). The skill makes a Settings Update Conditional but gives no guidance on whether 'already met' can be claimed or ruled out, although DE sample orgs often ship with Lead.NumberofLocations__c already mapped.

Rule 4 (share picklist values through a global value set) conflicts with minimal design here: promoting Lead.POS_System__c to a global value set makes it restricted, which changes behavior for other callers (a DMS integration has Edit). Step 5 lists a 'change that alters behavior for other callers' as an ask trigger, but the predict-the-answer rule says to decide when the data is empty. The skill does not say which rule wins.

No allowed query can confirm whether lead conversion enforces the converting user's FLS on mapped target fields. AskCoworker asserted it does. The skill has no rule for a platform behavior that is uncertain rather than documented, so it became a load-bearing assumption with a test case.

The validator requires every Conditional row to be named in Section 8 by API name. Referring to a dependent row by number ('row 8') failed the first pass. spec-format.md says to name it but does not say that a row-number reference is not enough.
Step 1 says to read .sf/config.json, but the RUNNER supplied the org alias. Both agreed (TestWriteSpecDE), so there was no conflict.
